<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Plan 190 shipped the writer and `pij directory add`. Roles exist but nobody holds them except in the hand-kept HOLDERS.md. This plan adds holding: assign and release, lineage, the close hook, the directory view, and the rulings that touch assignment (C1 seat roles, C6 queue-drain hook, C13/req-26 window names). Lineage lives on the governance branch, written through the plan 190 writer, and the store indexes it (migration 0031 pointers plus migration 0032), so `pij directory` gives the same answer after a store rebuild (req-17).

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A seat can take and leave a role with one verb each, and every holder is on record with its session and machine.
- Lineage is on the governance branch, so a store rebuild or another machine sees the same holders.
- Closing a seat ends its assignment without making close fail.
- `pij directory` shows this project's roles and their holders and nothing from another project.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Sending to a role and the role queue (s05). This plan only exposes the hook s05 uses (C6).
- Role templates and the core-role prompts (s03).
- Outputs, memory verbs and routing (s06 to s08).
- Starting seats: assign binds an existing live seat and never spawns one.

<a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Code facts (2026-11-04, main 6ccd4d8): seats table in crates/store/migrations/0001_init.sql:15-36 (harness session serialised as `session`, crates/core/src/model.rs:348-376; machine is a read projection, not stored per row). seat_roles (seat, role, assigned_by, assigned_at) in 0004_orchestration.sql:48-53, written via crates/store/src/role_assertion.rs. Close: CLI crates/cli/src/lifecycle.rs:9-20 posts /v1/close; handler crates/daemon/src/http/lifecycle.rs:241-348 calls registry.tombstone_if_unchanged; publish_tombstone in crates/store/src/registry.rs:48-99 is the one path for close, reap and revive. Project resolution: project_and_repo in crates/daemon/src/http/directory.rs:331-380. Pointer rebuild: crates/daemon/src/community/pointer.rs:20-85 (from_branch_head). Directory argv is forwarded to the daemon parser (crates/cli/src/governance.rs:14-28, crates/daemon/src/http/directory.rs:55-115), which is why --help fails. Window name is set only at spawn (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1330-1337, crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:1528); the control client supports rename (crates/tmux/src/control.rs:595-598). Latest migration 0031; migrations registered by sqlx migrate! (crates/store/src/migrate.rs:38).

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A close blocked or slowed by a governance write. | Medium | High | AC4: close never fails on the directory; pending ends are flushed by the next write. |
| Lineage and the store disagree after a crash between commit and store write. | Low | Medium | The branch is the authority; rebuild (AC8) restores the store; persist before mutate (P9). |
| Renaming a window confuses a human working in it. | Low | Low | Only on assign, once; the name says what the seat does. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
- Builds scoped with -p. Check `df -h /System/Volumes/Data` before a large build; stop and tell pm-001 under 25 GB. Reuse your existing target dir.
- No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`, never push refs/notes/*. No node_modules: TS proof is CI on the exact head.
- One push per review round; no pushes after a PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
